From 5ad6af5c91e9b942c44b657122270d935db3a813 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Feb 2024 15:17:14 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] drm/xe: Assume large page size if VMA not yet bound

The calculation to determine max page size of a VMA during a REMAP
operations assumes the VMA has been bound. This assumption is not true
if the VMA is from an eariler operation in an array of binds. If a VMA
has not been bound use the maximum page size which will ensure the
previous / next REMAP operations are not incorrectly skipped.

Fixes: 8f33b4f054fc ("drm/xe: Avoid doing rebinds")
Signed-off-by: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Rodrigo Vivi <rodrigo.vivi@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240205231714.2956225-1-matthew.brost@intel.com

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_vm.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_vm.c
index 7e29b816c4d4..ed594fa2f8da 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_vm.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_vm.c
@@ -2200,8 +2200,10 @@ static u64 xe_vma_max_pte_size(struct xe_vma *vma)
 		return SZ_1G;
 	else if (vma->gpuva.flags & XE_VMA_PTE_2M)
 		return SZ_2M;
+	else if (vma->gpuva.flags & XE_VMA_PTE_4K)
+		return SZ_4K;
 
-	return SZ_4K;
+	return SZ_1G;	/* Uninitialized, used max size */
 }
 
 static u64 xe_vma_set_pte_size(struct xe_vma *vma, u64 size)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_vm.c`**
   - The function `xe_vma_max_pte_size` has been modified to change the logic for determining the maximum page size of a Virtual Memory Area (VMA).
   - An additional condition has been added to check if the VMA has the flag `XE_VMA_PTE_4K`. If this flag is set, the function now returns `SZ_4K`.
   - The default return value has been changed from `SZ_4K` to `SZ_1G` for uninitialized VMAs, ensuring that the maximum page size is used when the VMA is not yet bound.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `xe_vma_max_pte_size` addresses a bug related to the assumption that a VMA is bound during REMAP operations. By ensuring that the maximum page size is returned for uninitialized VMAs, the patch prevents potential issues where subsequent REMAP operations could be incorrectly skipped. This change is directly related to the fix for the bug identified in the previous commit (`8f33b4f054fc`), which aimed to avoid unnecessary rebinds. The new logic ensures that the system behaves correctly even when VMAs are not yet bound, thereby enhancing the reliability of the REMAP operations.

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the incorrect assumption that a Virtual Memory Area (VMA) is always bound during REMAP operations. If a VMA is from an earlier operation in an array of binds and has not yet been bound, the calculation for the maximum page size does not account for this, leading to potential skipping of subsequent REMAP operations. This can result in improper memory management and allocation issues.

Here is the patch:
 
 static u64 xe_vma_max_pte_size(struct xe_vma *vma)
 {
 	if (vma->gpuva.flags & XE_VMA_PTE_1G)
 		return SZ_1G;
 	else if (vma->gpuva.flags & XE_VMA_PTE_2M)
 		return SZ_2M;
+	else if (vma->gpuva.flags & XE_VMA_PTE_4K)
+		return SZ_4K;
 
-	return SZ_4K;
+	return SZ_1G;	/* Uninitialized, used max size */
 }
